title: World Youth Championships day seven: Wen Ruibo and Jiang Yiyi win third golds as Hochart beats Yao Ruixuan
seo_title: World Youth Championships day 7: China win both doubles
description: World Youth Championships day seven: Wen Ruibo and Jiang Yiyi won third golds in the U19 doubles, and Leana Hochart beat Yao Ruixuan from 2-0 down.
standfirst: China won both under-19 doubles finals against South Korea, while Li Hechen gained revenge on Emanuel Otalvaro and Aditya Sareen won a seven-game quarter-final 11-1 in the decider.
body: Wen Ruibo and Jiang Yiyi won their third gold medals of the World Youth Championships in Istanbul on Friday, taking the under-19 doubles titles with their China teammates, while France's Leana Hochart came from two games down to knock Yao Ruixuan out of the girls' singles.

China have now won all five under-19 titles decided this week, the two team events, the mixed doubles and both doubles, and Wen and Jiang can each win a fourth in Saturday's singles. Hochart, ranked 227th, plays Japan's Mao Takamori for a place in the girls' final, and Australia's Aditya Sareen reached the boys' semi-finals after winning the seventh game of the longest under-19 match of the day 11-1.
## Two doubles finals, two Chinese titles

Jiang and Yao, the second seeds, beat South Korea's top seeds Jeong Yein and Heo Yerim 11-6, 11-9, 7-11, 11-9 in 32 minutes. A day earlier they had lost the first two games of their semi-final to Japan; this time they led from the start, and Jeong and Heo's only game came when they won the third 11-7.

Wen and Li Hechen, the top seeds, were quicker still. They beat Kim Daehwan and Lee Hyeonho, both 16 and seeded 12th, 11-7, 11-9, 11-4 in 21 minutes. The Korean pair took their timeout but won only four points in the last game.

For Wen, 19 and the world No 14, it was a third title after the boys' team event and the mixed doubles. Jiang, who turned 16 last week, has the same three. Li and Yao have two golds each, plus the mixed doubles silver they won against their teammates on Thursday.
## Hochart turns round Yao

Yao, the sixth seed and world No 160, won the first two games 11-4 and 11-5 and looked set for a third Chinese semi-final. Hochart, 18, won the third 11-9 and then the next three, 11-8, 11-7 and 11-6, to win in 45 minutes. It was a second straight win over a seed for the Frenchwoman, who had beaten Hong Kong's fourth seed Su Tsz Tung on Thursday. Yao, who had come from 3-0 down in the last 16, was the only one of China's four singles quarter-finalists to lose.

Jiang needed seven games to get past Taiwan's fifth seed Wu Ying Syuan. She won the first two games for the loss of seven points, then lost the next three 11-5, 11-9 and 11-8. Jiang won the last two 11-2 and 11-4, dropping six points, after 48 minutes. She now meets Egypt's Hana Goda, the world No 21 and highest-ranked woman in Istanbul, who swept India's Divyanshi Bhowmick 11-6, 11-8, 14-12, 12-10. Takamori, the second seed, beat Syndrela Das 11-7, 11-9, 11-7, 12-10, so neither Indian reached the semi-finals.
## Li gains his Dakar revenge

Li beat Colombia's second seed Emanuel Otalvaro 11-13, 11-8, 11-9, 10-12, 11-7, 11-6, reversing the [Youth Olympic Games quarter-final in Dakar](/news/youth-olympic-games-dakar-2026-otalvaro-beats-li-hechen-china-no-medal.html) this month that left China without a table tennis medal at the Games for the first time. Otalvaro, 16 and ranked 106th, took the first game in deuce and levelled at 2-2 by winning the fourth 12-10, but Li, 17 and the world No 177, won the last two games in 47 minutes.

Wen had no trouble in the rematch of Monday's team final decider. He beat Taiwan's Hung Che-Yen 11-7, 11-7, 11-4, 11-7 in 28 minutes, the shortest under-19 singles of the day. He plays Japan's Shunto Iwaida, 17, who beat Tunisia's Wassim Essid 11-6, 7-11, 11-7, 11-3, 11-3.
## Sareen's 11-1 decider

Sareen and Antoine Noirault, the two unseeded quarter-finalists, played for an hour and a minute. Noirault, who had beaten Hong Kong's fourth seed Li Ki Ho on Thursday, led 1-0 and 2-1 but lost the second and fifth games 13-11. He forced a seventh by winning the sixth 11-8, but Sareen, 18 and the world No 112, won the decider 11-1. He plays Li in the semi-finals.

Sareen and Hochart are the only semi-finalists from outside Asia and Africa. As in the doubles, there is no third-place match, so both are sure of at least a bronze medal; Hochart already has one from the girls' doubles.
## Results in full
Boys' singles, quarter-finals (seeds in brackets):

- Wen Ruibo (CHN, 1) bt Hung Che-Yen (TPE, 12) 11-7, 11-7, 11-4, 11-7
- Shunto Iwaida (JPN, 13) bt Wassim Essid (TUN) 11-6, 7-11, 11-7, 11-3, 11-3
- Aditya Sareen (AUS) bt Antoine Noirault (FRA) 7-11, 13-11, 7-11, 11-8, 13-11, 8-11, 11-1
- Li Hechen (CHN, 6) bt Emanuel Otalvaro (COL, 2) 11-13, 11-8, 11-9, 10-12, 11-7, 11-6
Girls' singles, quarter-finals:

- Jiang Yiyi (CHN, 1) bt Wu Ying Syuan (TPE, 5) 11-3, 11-4, 5-11, 9-11, 8-11, 11-2, 11-4
- Hana Goda (EGY, 3) bt Divyanshi Bhowmick (IND, 8) 11-6, 11-8, 14-12, 12-10
- Leana Hochart (FRA, 15) bt Yao Ruixuan (CHN, 6) 4-11, 5-11, 11-9, 11-8, 11-7, 11-6
- Mao Takamori (JPN, 2) bt Syndrela Das (IND) 11-7, 11-9, 11-7, 12-10
Doubles finals:

- Girls' doubles: Jiang Yiyi / Yao Ruixuan (CHN, 2) bt Jeong Yein / Heo Yerim (KOR, 1) 11-6, 11-9, 7-11, 11-9
- Boys' doubles: Wen Ruibo / Li Hechen (CHN, 1) bt Kim Daehwan / Lee Hyeonho (KOR, 12) 11-7, 11-9, 11-4
## Saturday: semi-finals and finals

The last day starts at about 8.30am UK time with the boys' semi-finals, Wen against Iwaida and Sareen against Li. Jiang plays Goda and Hochart plays Takamori at about 9.15am. The boys' final is at about 2pm and the girls' final at about 2.45pm. Times are approximate. Eleven's [event page](/events/world-youth-championships-2026.html#matches) has live scores and the draws, and the [day seven preview](/news/world-youth-championships-2026-day-seven-preview-order-of-play.html) has more on the players.
